title: Dedicated GPU Stewardship Panel — Predictive Throttle & QoS Editor
creator: Maya Chen
description: Purpose: Design a compact, operator-focused panel for Redwood Console that surfaces per-reserve health signals, predictive congestion forecasts, and an inline QoS/throttle editor to tune request shaping for Dedicated GPU reservations. This UI is intended for platform owners and SREs who manage Dedicated capacity pools. Goals: 1) provide an at-a-glance health summary combining utilization, latency P95/P99 trends, and KV cache hit-rate; 2) surface short-term capacity pressure forecasts (15/60/240 min) based on telemetry and recent request patterns; 3) allow operators to create and apply QoS presets and soft throttle rules (percent-of-pool, priority-class weights, fallback model routing) without leaving the console; 4) include safety guardrails (preview impact simulation and an undo window) and link to rollout/incident playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Compact panel renders in dedicated reserve detail view with health summary, forecast sparkline, and QoS editor button
Forecast algorithm placeholder visualized (15/60/240min) with confidence band; engineers can replace with real service data
QoS editor supports: create/edit preset, set percent-of-pool cap, assign priority weight, define fallback model route
Preview mode simulates estimated pct change to latency and throughput using historical sample; simulation available before apply
Apply flow includes canary toggle (10%/25%/50%) and automatic rollback within a configurable window
Design annotated with accessibility contrast and keyboard flows; responsive down to 1024px width
Figma prototype linked and usability-tested with at least 3 SRE/platform leads; feedback loop documented
Handoff artifacts include token-level cost impact estimate template for PM/ENG to fill

Updated copy and added 'undo within 15m' microcopy.

decisions: Use a compact horizontal strip in the reserve detail page rather than a full-page module to reduce context switching for operators
Expose only curated QoS controls in the initial release (percent cap, priority weight, fallback model) to avoid overwhelming users; advanced rule editor deferred
Show forecast as 3 horizons (15m/60m/240m) with confidence band; if input metrics missing, show 'degraded forecast' annotation
Include simulation/preview mode as required safety step before applying any live throttle rules
Canary rollout options will be 10%, 25%, 50% for MVP with explicit rollback window default of 15 minutes
